purpose: Primary formal graph-module theorem, concrete nonconstant rank-two projective connection, and explicit finite-admission boundary; no bounded-lift claim.

primary_source.title: Quantization of Vector Bundles on Lagrangian Subvarieties
primary_source.inspected_version: Author-hosted 2017 journal advance PDF, 22 pages; accepted 6 September 2017; download stamp 3 November 2017. Not identified with arXiv:1701.01542v1.
exact_locations: Printed pages 1-2: formal quantization and flat h-complete module definition.
Theorem 1.1, printed page 4: higher period restrictions, flat projectivization, and refined first Chern equality.
Theorem 5.1, printed pages 15-16: chosen flat PGL_r(k[[h]]) datum and compatible Picard-algebroid module in the successive lifting construction.
Section 6 first remark, printed page 19: parameter-module sheaf identification E_h with E[[h]] when Y is affine.
primary_source.inspection: Internal AI-assisted reading of the primary web PDF and local pypdf extraction of the cached exact bytes. Root independently inspected the same author PDF theorem and completeness definition.
actual_import: Formal quantization existence under Theorem 1.1's three conditions.
Theorem 5.1 permits retention of a chosen compatible flat formal projective bundle.
Affine Y allows a parameter-module sheaf identification, without an uncompleted source-module finiteness assertion.
application_hypotheses_checked: The graph of a polynomial symplectic endomorphism is a smooth closed Lagrangian in target times opposite source; its source projection is an isomorphism without an inverse map premise.
The ambient product has the standard formal Weyl/Moyal quantization.
The graph is affine space, has trivial canonical bundle, and has zero degree-two algebraic de Rham and truncated de Rham cohomology.
The trivial rank-two bundle has zero first Chern class and the explicit polynomial flat connection in the note; its formal projective connection is extended constantly in h.
The Picard algebroid has zero refined class, so a splitting makes the selected flat connection a compatible module datum.
excluded_imports: No finite PBW support, actual source finite-projective algebraization, or nonzero-parameter specialization theorem is imported.
No scalar Weyl realization, invariant scalar quantum carrier, arithmetic support compatibility, or DC1/DC2 implication is imported.

written_arguments: Polynomial symplectic graphs meet the primary theorem's geometric and cohomological hypotheses.
The rank-two polynomial connection d-[[0,1],[X,0]]dX is flat and trace zero.
A rational invariant line would give w'+w^2=X; integer degree at infinity excludes every rational w over the field of the other coordinates, also after constant extension.
The elementary Airy matrix Weyl embedding is strict for Bernstein PBW degree; first-h-order induction preserves and reflects a uniform PBW support bound on scalar formal series.
Consequently composing an existing scalar formal lift with this elementary embedding cannot repair unbounded support. Other graph-module realizations are not asserted to be compositional.
existing_result_boundary: Rank-one formal graph existence is already recorded in PROOF.md via Baranovsky-Ginzburg-Kaledin-Pecharich Theorem 1.1.4; no new scalar formal-existence claim is made.
checker_scope: No new finite checker; primary-source inspection and written proofs are the retained evidence.
remaining_gap: Actual finite-PBW graph bimodule with admitted global target actions, finite projective/free source realization and a uniform PBW bound; any scalar realization and prescribed arithmetic support remain separate unproved steps.
